# The image domain

Image documents: layers, text, shapes, templates with slots, export to PNG, JPEG or WebP.

## How to reach it

MCP tools: `edit`, `command_help`, `history`, `image`. Tools that take `domain=image`: `edit`, `command_help`, `history`.

CLI: `stuarty image` lists the commands of the domain and `stuarty image <verb>` runs one; the full names stay valid.

- `image:create`: create an image document, blank or from a template
- `image:list`: list the image documents and templates
- `image:show`: describe an image document: its layers, its findings and its revision
- `image:edit`: apply a batch of image operations (stuarty command:help --domain image lists them)
- `image:undo`: undo the last step of the caller on an image
- `image:redo`: redo the last undone step of the caller on an image
- `image:export`: export an image document to a PNG, JPEG or WebP file
- `image:import`: bring an image file into a new image document, or into an existing one as a layer
- `image:revert`: go back to the document of an earlier revision of an image, as a new step that image:undo takes back
- `image:diff`: list what changed between two revisions of an image, most significant first
- `image:checkpoint:create`: name a revision of an image so that it can be gone back to
- `image:checkpoint:list`: list the checkpoints of an image, newest revision first
- `image:checkpoint:rename`: rename a checkpoint of an image, and change its note
- `image:checkpoint:remove`: remove a checkpoint of an image; no revision is removed

## Operations

These 27 operations go in the `operations` of `edit` with `domain=image`, grouped by namespace; `command_help domain=image` lists them with their summaries and `command_help name=<operation> domain=image` gives the arguments of one.

- `canvas`: resize
- `image`: create
- `layer`: add_fill, add_image, add_shape, add_text, adjust, align, blend, crop, duplicate, filter_add, filter_move, filter_remove, filter_set, fit, group, mask_clear, mask_set, move, remove, replace_source, set, set_shape, set_text, transform, ungroup
